title: Preflight Deploy Scrapbook: quick checks & pin heuristics
content:
Notes-to-self: this is my small, messy checklist for preflight and quick-pin options. Put in the bits I repeatedly forget and the micro-scripts I run when I'm on-call. Not a canonical playbook — just the first-10-minutes checklist for a rollout that must stay up.

High-level goal:
- Push minor runtime/model change with minimal blast radius. Start canary -> observe 5–10 minutes -> expand or pin/rollback. Keep users on stable model if anything smells.

Quick preflight (local):
- sanity: curl localhost:8080/health -> 200 (latency < 50ms typical)
- smoke gen: echo 'tight test prompt' | curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d @- and check tokens, no OOM, no nan
- kvcache: check /metrics kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0 for warm workloads
- binary size/quant: ./tools/check-quant.sh model-v2.3.1-quant -> expected size 3.6G

Console checks (Redwood Console):
- open model route dashboard -> slow tails and 99th pct should not spike on previous 1h
- trace a sample request (trace id from smoke run) -> ensure correct kernel path used
- cost per token for canary model vs stable: if >1.25x, ask product for approval

Canary plan (example):
- step 0 (warmup): run 50 synthetic requests at target seq len, confirm steady latency
- step 1 (5% traffic, 20m) -> watch error_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99, and quality using golden prompt set
- step 2 (20% traffic, 30m) -> check infrastructure metrics and rollout KPI
- step 3 (50% traffic, 30m) -> manual approval to 100% or pin fallback

Pin heuristics (when to force-pin stable):
- auto-pin if quality regression on golden set > 3% (precision/bleu depending on test)
- manual pin if p99 latency exceeds SLA by >25% for >10m
- immediate pin if error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m or any critical errors (OOM, crash loops)

Commands I use often (keep here):
- create canary route: redwoodctl route create --name canary-ks --model model-v2.3.1-quant --traffic 0.05 --region us-west1
- adjust traffic: redwoodctl route update canary-ks --traffic 0.20
- pin stable: redwoodctl route pin stable-route --model model-v2.3.0
- quick rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --route canary-ks --to stable-route --reason "auto-fail: p99"

Emergency fallback patterns (fast answers for pager):
- immediate mitigation: redirect 100% traffic to last-known-good route: redwoodctl route update stable-route --traffic 1.0
- if infra fault: scale up Dedicated pool temporarily (if quota) and set route priority to dedicated
- temporary client-side mitigation: enable token-throttling or reduce max_tokens in proxy for heavy endpoints

Observability anchors to watch during canary:
- active_shards, gpu_util, nv_mem_free, kv_cache_hit_ratio, request_queuing_ms, model_error_rate, user-facing latency p99
- golden-prompt-quality: run the quick eval harness every 5m (script below)

Quick eval harness (local):
- python infra/tools/eval_harness.py --route canary-ks --set golden_prompts.json --output tmp/eval.json --thresholds config/eval-thresholds.yaml
- if eval_harness reports > allowed_regression (see config), immediately pin

Small heuristics I keep forgetting:
- warmup matters more than you think for KV-heavy models — run a 2k token warmup sequence rather than a few 512s
- quantized variants can hide rare correctness regressions in long-context chains
- route bleed: always set a hard guard (max_traffic=0.5) on automated ramps to prevent runaway expansion

Open questions / TODOs:
- make a tiny script that does: deploy -> heat -> eval -> auto-pin-if-good (opt-in toggle)
- check legal/CS for high-risk customers before canary on global traffic (need list)
- confirm with infra if we have emergency GPU spare capacity in us-east1 for rapid fallback

Postmortem notes template (if canary fails):
- timeline (minute precision)
- triggered alerts and who ack'd them
- degraded metrics vs baseline
- root cause hypothesis and reproducer steps
- follow-ups (owners + due dates)

End notes: this doc is intentionally scrappy. Keep the commands up-to-date and move stable patterns into the shared playbook once we validate them across 2 releases. If you copy-paste anything, triple-check route names and regions first.

Sana K.
